name: Sikafloor®-160
tagline: 2-part epoxy primer, levelling mortar, intermediate layer and mortar screed
summary: Sikafloor®-160 is an economic, two part, low viscosity epoxy resin. "Total solid epoxy composition according to the test method Deutsche Bauchemie e.V. (German Association for construction chemicals)"
metaDescription: Sikafloor®-160 is an economic, two part, low viscosity epoxy resin. "Total solid epoxy composition according to the test method Deutsche Bauchemie e.V. (German Association for construction chemicals)"
usage: For priming concrete substrates, cement screeds and epoxy mortars
For low to medium absorbent substrates
Primer for a varity of Sikafloor MultiDur and MultiFlex flooring systems
Binder for levelling mortars and mortar screeds
packaging: Part A | 7.1 kg containers Part B | 4.0 kg containers Part A+B | 11.1 kg ready to mix units Part A | 20 KG drums Part B | 20 KG drums

items.label: SUSTAINABILITY
items.text: LEED Rating Sikafloor®-160 conforms to the requirements of LEED EQ Credit 4.2: Low-Emitting Materials: Paints & Coatings SCAQMD Method 304-91 VOC Content < 100 g/l

items.label: APPROVALS / CERTIFICATES
items.text:
Epoxy primer, levelling mortar and mortar screed according to EN 1504-2: 2004 and EN 13813:2002, DoP 02 08 01 02 050 0 000021 1008, certified by Factory Production Control Body No. 0921 and provided with the CE-mark.
“Products and systems for the protection and repair of concrete structures–Test method – Compatibility on wet concrete when exposed to the effects of humidity from the rear” according to the DIN EN 13578:2004.Proof statement P 9400-E

items.label: Composition
items.text: Epoxy

items.label: Shelf life
items.text: 12 months from date of production

items.label: Storage conditions
items.text: The packaging must be stored properly in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging, in dry conditions at temperatures between +5°C and +30°C.

items.label: Density
items.text:
Part A | ~ 1.13 kg/l
Part B | ~ 1.02 kg/l
Mixed Resin | ~ 1.10 kg/l
All density values at +23°C

items.label: Compressive strength
items.text: Mortar Screed: >35 N/mm² (28 days / +23°C / 50 % r.h.) | (EN13892-2)

items.label: Tensile strength in flexure
items.text: Mortar Screed: ~15 N/mm² (28 days / +23°C / 50 % r.h.) | (EN13892-2)

items.label: Tensile adhesion strength
items.text: > 1.5 N/mm² (failure in concrete) | (ISO 4624)

items.label: Temperature resistance
items.text:
Exposure* | Dry heat
Permanent | +50°C
Short-term max. 7 d | +80°C
Short-term max. 12 h | +100°C
Short-term moist/wet heat* up to +80°C where exposure is only occasional (steam cleaning etc.).
*No simultaneous chemical and mechanical exposure and only in combination with Sikafloor® systems as a broadcast system with approx. 3 - 4 mm thickness.

items.label: Mixing ratio
items.text: Part A : Part B = 64 : 36 (by weight) 1.6:1 (by volume)

items.label: Ambient air temperature
items.text: +10°C min. / +30°C max.

items.label: Relative air humidity
items.text: 80 % r.h. max.

items.label: Dew point
items.text:
Beware of condensation! The substrate and uncured floor must be at least 3°C above dew point to reduce the risk of condensation or blooming on the floor finish.
Note: Low temperatures and high humidity conditions increase the probability of blooming.

items.label: Substrate temperature
items.text: +10°C min. / +30°C max.

items.label: Substrate moisture content
items.text:
Maximum 4% when measures using Sika® - Tramex meter ( at the time of application). Please note that the moisture content must be < 4 % pbw when using the CM measurement or Oven-dry-method.
No rising moisture according to ASTM (Polyethylene-sheet).

items.label: Pot Life
items.text:
Temperature | Time
+10°C | ~50 minutes
+20°C | ~25 minutes
+30°C | ~15 minutes

items.label: Curing time
items.text:
Before applying solvent free products on Sikafloor®-160 allow:
Substrate temperature | Minimum | Maximum
+10°C | 24 hours | 4 days
+20°C | 12 hours | 2 days
+30°C | 8 hours | 24 hours
Before applying solvent containing products on Sikafloor®-160 allow:
Substrate temperature | Minimum | Maximum
+10°C | 36 hours | 6 days
+20°C | 24 hours | 4 days
+30°C | 16 hours | 2 days
Times are approximate and will be affected by changing ambient conditions particularly temperature and relative humidity.

items.label: Consumption
items.text:
Coating System | Product | Consumption
Priming | 1 - 2 x Sikafloor®-160 | 1 - 2 x 0.25 - 0.50 kg/m²
Levelling mortar fine (surface roughness < 1 mm) | 1 pbw Sikafloor®-160 + 0.5 pbw quartz sand (0.1 - 0.3 mm) | 1.4 kg/m²/mm
Levelling mortar medium (surface roughness up to 2 mm) | 1 pbw Sikafloor®-160 + 1 pbw quartz sand (0.1 - 0.3 mm) | 1.6 kg/m²/mm)
Intermediate layer (self-smoothing 1.5 to 3 mm) | 1 pbw Sikafloor®-160 + 1 pbw quartz sand (0.1 - 0.3 mm) | 1.6 kg/m²/mm
+ optional broadcast quartz sand 0.4 – 0.7 mm | ~ 4.0 kg/m²
Bonding bridge | 1 - 2 x Sikafloor®-160 | 1- 2 x 0.3 - 0.5 kg/m²
Epoxy screed (15 - 20 mm layer thickness ) / Repair Mortar | 1 pbw Sikafloor®-160 + 8 pbw quartz sand | 2.2 kg/m²/mm
Note: These figures are theoretical and do not allow for any additional material required due to surface porosity, surface profile, variations in level or wastage etc.

items.label: MIXING
items.text:
Prior to mixing, stir part A mechanically. When all of part B has been added to part A, mix continuously for 3 minutes until a uniform mix has been achieved. When parts A and B have been mixed, add the quartz sand and if required the Extender T and mix for a further 2 minutes until a uniform mix has been achieved. To ensure thorough mixing pour materials into another container and mix again to achieve a consistent mix. Over mixing must be avoided to minimise air entrainment.
Mixing Tools
Sikafloor®-160 must be thoroughly mixed using a low speed electric stirrer (300 - 400 rpm) or other suitable equipment. For the preparation of mortars use a forced action mixer of rotating pan, paddle or trough type. Free fall mixers should not be used.

items.label: APPLICATION
items.text: Prior to application, confirm substrate moisture content, relative air humidity and dew point. If > 4% pbw moisture content, Sikafloor® EpoCem® may be applied as a T.M.B. (temporary moisture barrier) system. Primer: Make sure a continuous, pore free coat covers the substrate. If necessary, apply two priming coats. Apply Sikafloor®-160 by brush, roller or squeegee. Preferred application is by using a squeegee and then backrolling crosswise. Levelling mortar: Rough surfaces need to be levelled first. Apply the levelling mortar by squeegee/trowel to the required thickness. Intermediate layer: Sikafloor®-160 is poured, spread evenly by means of a serrated trowel. Roll immediately in two directions with spiked roller to ensure even thickness and if required broadcast with quartz sand, after about 15 minutes (at +20°C) but before 30 minutes (at+20°C), at first lightly and then to excess. Bonding bridge: Apply Sikafloor®-160 by brush, roller or squeegee. Preferred application is by using a squeegee and then backrolling crosswise. Epoxy screed / repair mortar: Apply the mortar screed evenly on the still “tacky” bonding bridge, using levelling battens and screed rails as necessary. After a short waiting time compact and smoothen the mortar with a trowel or Teflon coated power float (usually 20 - 90 rpm).

items.label: CLEANING OF EQUIPMENT
items.text: Clean all tools and application equipment with Thinner C immediately after use. Hardened and/or cured material can only be removed mechanically.
